utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen, the technical booth, the interpreters; good morning, legal assistants and court reporters; good morning to the Prosecution, Ms. Hollis and Mr. Waidyaratne; good morning to the Defence. I see we're all present. Good morning to the accused. We're going to resume our hearing. Have the witness brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me? Can you hear me, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Are you feeling well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to remind you that you are continuing to testify under oath, and today you are going to answer questions by the Defence attorneys. Mr. Krstan Simic, what is the order for the cross-examination. I can see that you will be the first.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. The cross-examination will be in the order in which the accused are listed in the indictment, but the representatives of Mr. Kos have no questions. So we will follow the order with the exception of the Defence team for Mr. Kos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Thank you very much, Mr. Simic. You may begin. You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Mrkalj.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: We will be talking today about a number of issues, and I hope we will be able to clarify a certain number of things. During your testimony yesterday you said that you graduated from the School of Internal Affairs; it is a secondary level school in Sarajevo. Upon graduation, were you obliged to do your regular military service?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Regardless of the fact that you were under no obligation to do your regular military service, were you duty-bound as a military conscript to report to the competent Defence Ministry, or one of its departments depending on your place of residence?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you clear up exactly what you mean? Could you clarify that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: As an able-bodied man, of age, were you duty-bound to report to the competent military authorities as a military conscript, to be listed?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The records were kept automatically, because upon graduation my military service was automatically recognised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me for interrupting you. Witness, are you having a problem? Is something wrong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, a little. I have a bit of a headache but we can continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you sure? Are you capable of continuing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, I'll try.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you say you are capable, then there is nothing I can do. Mr. Simic, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: You were not obliged to serve in the army, but were you a conscript, according to the laws in force in Yugoslavia at the time?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: When you were working in Belgrade, in which municipality were you recorded as a military conscript?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you already, that was done automatically and I was in the municipality of Savski Vijenac. I didn't have to report myself; I was listed automatically.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: In 1988 you started working in the municipality of Prijedor, which is another municipality and another republic in Yugoslavia at the time. Did you report your change of address to the municipality in which you said you had been automatically registered?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: As a military conscript; that's what we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a military conscript. All this is done automatically. All my documents were transferred to Prijedor municipality, to the public security station and to the military department. My only responsibility was to report my new address.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you get a wartime assignment in Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher distribute these copies for Their Honours, the Prosecution, and the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is there a problem with the English translation? No?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The English translation will be D27/1A, and in B/C/S, D27/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mrkalj, you have in front of you a certificate of the Defence Ministry, Prijedor department, in which it says that: "Edin Mrkalj, son of Husein, born on the 13th of June, after the Savski Vijenac municipality in Belgrade, reported on the 13th of December, 1977 to the Military Department," and that your military duties were linked to the public security station in Prijedor as a policeman. It is also stated that you had the military speciality number "11.107, policeman," without any superior position which, in wartime conditions, is the equivalent to a foot soldier. Is that correct? Your military obligation when you moved to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you, I didn't go to the military department. This was automatic. In order to get employment, this was done automatically.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mrkalj, you spoke frequently yesterday about rules and procedures. You're a policeman; you have a military obligation. When war breaks out, what would you do? Were you given a military assignment telling you what you should do automatically?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but in the case of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: That is my question. Is this your military assignment in the case of war?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that case, I am a military policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: An ordinary policeman?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, a military policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: But in terms of rank, a regular military police officer? Would you have a rank? Would you be in charge?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: So your speciality number is 11.107, equals policeman, equals soldier, equals military policeman.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you said. I have no idea what all this means, this "VES," and "policeman," and "soldier."

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mrkalj, how would you know what you should do should such a situation arise?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, I would probably be given an order and then I would know what I should do in such a situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mrkalj. Yesterday you mentioned that when you arrived in Omarska, that you had known from before your colleagues, policemen, even some who had graduated from the same school as you, including Mr. Kvocka and Mr. Meakic, who, for a time, went to the same school at the same time as you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: You also said yesterday that the police service was organised, that there was a police station in Prijedor, and that there were three departments or sections of the police station; one in Kozarac, another in Ljubija, and a third department of the police station was in Omarska. Did you ever work as a policeman in a department of the police station?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: My question is: Did you or did you not?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I know that you were linked to the police station.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. As a policeman you had to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: So you didn't work in a department, in the police station department ever, anywhere. Do you know how such a department is organised; the number of personnel, the commander, and how the other services are organised?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew most of the people who worked in those departments.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the people, I'm asking you about the organisation.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was familiar with that organisational structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: On the basis of what?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you go to school, then we have practical training, and when you're doing this practical training, you have to go through all the various departments, including police station departments, and you have to know how such a department functions. So that I was familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in which of these police organisations was Mr. Kvocka employed, and in which Mr. Meakic?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking what post they personally held. They were linked to Omarska. And I think Kvocka to Kozarac, but partly also to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about 1991 and 1992. Where did these two gentlemen work, Mr. Meakic and Mr. Kvocka, in which police station?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I think I was in Omarska. Omarska. You go on asking, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the status of Mr. Kvocka and Mr. Meakic was in 1991 and 1992?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that they had been promoted, but exactly to what, I cannot recollect. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mrkalj, yesterday you tried hard to show us your knowledge about the organisation of the police, so please tell us, if you can -- if you cannot, no problem -- what positions exist in a police station department?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is the chief of the station --

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Please give us the official title because, after all, we are jurists here.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So he would be the commander of the police station department.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Then?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then he would have a deputy and then, depending on the number of sectors or departments, the structure would go downwards for that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: So to round this question off, there was a commander, a deputy, and departments and sectors that were operating; is that so?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mrkalj, how many personnel does a police station department have?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That depends on the area covered by such a department.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the departments in Omarska, Ljubija, Kozarac. Do you know the number or not? We're talking about departments in a local community.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you what it says in the rules. The number of personnel depends on the needs, and that depends on the territory covered by that department. So it is not specified whether the number should be 10, 15, 20, or 30.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mrkalj, we are talking about Prijedor Police Station departments. As you worked in the Prijedor Police Station, do you know how many people were employed in the police station department in Omarska?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number because there were changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday, talking about this subject, you said that Mr. Kvocka wore a blue camouflage police uniform; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Ms. Hollis, in her examination, showed you a regular police camouflage uniform and you said that Mr. Kvocka wore just such a uniform.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat the basic colour of this camouflage uniform worn by the police?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main colour?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: You had a photograph in front of you.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Pale blue. Blue, with spots so as to make it multicoloured. Dark blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I see. Dark blue. Yes, that's fine. Mr. Meakic, did he wear a police uniform?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, did he or didn't he?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What kind of uniform? Was it the regular uniform or a camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wore, I don't know how we used to call it in those days, a polygon shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Is the same kind of shirt as the person shown on the photograph shown to you yesterday?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, he would change shirts. He would wear a blue one and a camouflage one and -- it depended. They didn't attach importance to uniformity.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Let us clear that up a little. Does that mean that Mr. Meakic, while in Omarska, wore a regular police uniform and a camouflage police uniform and he switched from one to the other?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What about the other policemen on duty to provide security?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were so many uniforms, different types, military, police, even civilian ones. For example, for the worst shift --

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you that, Witness. I'm asking you about uniforms?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm telling you about uniforms. For example, one individual had sports clothing with the number 3 on it, and then shift number 3, the worst shift, took on this number from that, the sports shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should now like to ask the usher to present the witness Exhibit 3/81, which has been tendered as an exhibit. It is a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Before you are shown the document, one more question. What is the difference between a military camouflage uniform and a police one? What's the basic difference?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, depending on the unit you belong to.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: We're talking about camouflage. Is it green, blue, red, what, the background?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were different ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Let's talk about the infantry uniforms.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I say, there were many different ones. I'm telling you -- I'm speaking about them in general.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about camouflage uniforms. But please have a look at the photograph that you have before you now?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's a classical military one.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: A classical military camouflage uniform; is that right? We agree? Mr. Mrkalj, can you identify the individuals wearing classical, regular military camouflage uniforms in the picture? Have a look. We have all the time in the world. The man with his arm raised.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I knew these people very well, but, you know what, I did know them very well but now --

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: You can't remember?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me just have a little time. I'll remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, just take it slowly.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Simo Drljaca, the one with his arm up, arm raised.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Very well. The second individual standing next to Simo Drljaca?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that once but I've forgotten. Whether I knew or didn't know, I really --

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's take the third individual standing behind the man wearing the army cap. Do you know him, the man behind?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: He looks familiar, sir, but I can't remember. Believe me when I say I just can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mrkalj.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to take note of the fact that Mr. Mrkalj has not identified the third individual from the man with the raised arm. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Let us now move on to another area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, let me ask you once again. Are you capable of continuing or not, or would you like us to take a break?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can. I'll say myself if I'm not able to continue, Your Honour. I don't feel well but let's get the job done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. If you're not in a state to continue -- the object is not to continue, the object is to be able to continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes, I thought of that too. But we can continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, please continue. If possible, ask direct questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We do have to go through things because the witness talked about many things that are included in the indictment -- that are not included in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises. Things that are not included.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you spoke at great length about rights and duties and the conduct of police officers in prisons, et cetera. I apologise to have to go back.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't matter. Just go ahead and ask me.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is an area that we're interested in, and we seemed to skim over them very quickly. Did you ever work in a prison as a guard?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: You didn't. In the former SFRY, and therefore in Bosnia-Herzegovina itself, were prisons organised as autonomous units, independent units? Was there a warden? Did the prison have a warden?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: In those prisons, were the detainees people who were in custody awaiting trial, as well as prisoners performing their sentence, their prison sentence?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that depended what prison you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: We're talking about the prison principle.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, that, once again, depends on the type of prison because there are different types of prisons.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I am talking about district prisons. For the Prijedor area, where was the district prison?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in the Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about for the Prijedor municipality. The prison for Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in Bihac.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In Bihac. Do you know if the police had any competence and authority in the organisation and supervision of prisons? Was the prison under the president of the district court, his authorisation, or was it under the CSB, the security services chief? Under whose authority? Or perhaps the Ministry of Justice.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I know you cannot. That is just why I wanted to ask you -- that is precisely why I asked you the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, without any comments, please. Please refrain from making comments. Just put your questions, because otherwise you're going to get into a discussion and debate with the witness. You cannot judge the answer of the witness. Just ask simple questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I apologise, but we seem to come across this problem time and again, that witnesses, during the cross-examination, this happened on previous occasions, try to avoid answers and try to give us explanations instead of answers, and we are conscious of the problems that arise but we'll try and avoid those problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, the answer "I do not know" is a valid answer. If the witness said, I do not know, then you cannot oblige him to give you the answer you would like to hear, neither can you judge the response given. So please refrain from that and ask questions, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that's what I want to hear. He said I don't know. Thank you. That's the answer I wanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: The police station that you worked in, I'm not speaking about your department but the whole station, what were the superiors, the superior officers of the station?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the police station of Prijedor? It had the chief of the SUP --

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Exclude the public security station. I'm speaking about the police station as part of the security system.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what you want. But I'm talking about structure, I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mrkalj, I am asking you the command structure in the police station of Prijedor. That's a simple and clear-cut question.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I'm giving you an answer, sir. At the top is the chief, the number one man, the chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I am talking about a part of the organisation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, please let the witness answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness is answering and telling me about a structure that I'm not asking him about. I assume that the witness, as a police officer, knows the structure better than I do because he was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, you asked him, at least that was the translation I got, what was the organigramme, and the witness answered that there was a commander, and he was about to continue when you interrupted him. So allow the witness to answer, please, if you would.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead, witness. Mr. Mrkalj, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you want me to tell you now?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Who was the number one man of the police station of Prijedor, the Prijedor Police Station?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief. The number one man was the chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The most responsible person.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you want us to continue with?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, next, did the station have a commander, a leader?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So you want me to tell you the organisation downwards? Very well. I understand now. We had the chief, as the number one man, and then according to structure, the police station was divided into the following: We had departments, the crime department, the public security department, we had the traffic department, and then a general department for administrative matters. What would you like to know now?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mrkalj, we don't seem to be establishing communication here, and it is very simple. In the testimonies, previous ones and now, we have been mentioning the SUP and the public security station. Is that the same thing?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean SUP?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: The secretariat of internal affairs, to put it in full.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how much -- how far you're acquainted with this. I'm acquainted with this very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, then you should know.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was working, the OSUP didn't exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: The OSUP didn't exist.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is to say, the public security has changed. At one point it was called the OSUP, the general secretariat of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, then, please tell me when this changed occurred.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Please tell me when these changes came into effect.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember when the changes took place, but I know that we were then -- we were called the public security station of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Was this while you were in Prijedor or while you were in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember. Believe me, it was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's go back now. Whether the OSUP and the public security station, are they one and the same thing? According to functioning, did they just change their name, change their heading? Were they actually the same thing?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I suppose they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Or were they not?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, just the title, the name changed. Everything else stayed the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Very well. You don't know when the organisation of the public security stations, as they became called, were introduced.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Now we're going to use the term "the public security station" to facilitate matters. I can see that you are not feeling well, but please do try and concentrate. The public security station of Prijedor, what did it consist of? What was its composition?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already enumerated.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, please try again because we seem to have mixed up the SUP and the public security station, so let's do it again, if you would, please.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The public security station became a general part for traffic safety, for crime. There was another department for state security, which was slightly separate. Then there was this general administrative department.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Within the frameworks of that SJB, the public security station, was there a police station, an Omarska police station? And we spoke about that. We discussed it all day yesterday.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The department --

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: No, I'm talking about the Prijedor police station. Was it within the composition of the SJB, the public security station? I seem to be unclear on this.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, it is within its composition.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Very well, then. What was the name of the superior, the number one man, in the police station of Prijedor, which is a component part of the SJB of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat that question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What was the name of the number one man of the Prijedor police station within the composition of the SJB station of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first man is the chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes. Let's skip over that. We've now come to this particular unit. The station itself.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the station or leader. Now, it depends who you're thinking of.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I'm thinking of the commander of the Prijedor police station. That's all.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the police station, Dule Jankovic, that was his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did he have a deputy?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did he have his assistants?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did he -- within the -- that is to say, we're now talking about the police station you worked in yourself. Was there a -- were there shifts, duty shifts?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Was there a duty officer? Were you ever the officer on duty, the duty officer?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean by "duty officer"?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, you explain to me. Did you ever perform the function of somebody who was on duty at the police station in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this term "on duty" or "duty" does not exist. I don't know what it means.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Was there no operative duty officer, officer on duty, whatever you like to call it?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, you don't know what it means. Thank you, then.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, would you please answer the questions put to you by the attorney.

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wish to ask you something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, please continue. Yes, witness, you wanted to say something? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot answer a question or a word or function that I don't know about, and that is why I say that this term "duty" or "on duty," I don't understand what is meant by it.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Mrkalj, we're going to try and simplify matters still further. If the station is open from 7.00 to 2.00 p.m., that's one shift, then there's another shift --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, excuse me, please. The witness said that he doesn't know what it means "duty" or "on duty." Why are you going to explain it to him? You are not the witness, Mr. Simic. Carry on. The witness says he doesn't know what "duty" or "on duty" means, so there's no need to go on explaining. Just move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mrkalj, I'm now going to talk for a minute about Omarska and ask you a question in that regard for a brief moment. You said yesterday that you had serious injuries inflicted on you by the fact that a pipe was placed in your mouth, your teeth were broken, so on and so forth. Was any assistance given to you in Omarska, medical treatment of any kind?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Did you ask for treatment? Did you ask anybody for treatment?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't in a position to.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. When you left Omarska --

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me. I didn't finish my answer. I wasn't in a position -- I was in a very poor condition. My condition was so poor that they had to carry me, and how could I ask for treatment --

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, but a few days later, perhaps. A few days later, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I was not allowed to breathe, let alone anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: When you left Omarska, did you apply for treatment anywhere, in a medical institution of any kind?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Where and when? What institution?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received treatment. I had my first surgical intervention in Croatia, in Karlovac, that is to say, when we left. And then in another country I had another surgical -- I underwent surgery for a second time. Then I had treatment, many years of treatment. After that I haven't --

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: I didn't ask you about psychiatric treatment. We'll come to that later on. I shall be happy to come to that later on but I'm asking you the other thing first. Mr. Mrkalj, have you retained any documents about your treatment, concerning your treatment, the treatment you underwent?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I do have the documents, yes, and that I could come by that documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Very well. Yesterday you said that when you arrived in Omarska that you knew Mr. Meakic as a colleague, Mr. Kvocka as well, and Mr. Radic, that you knew them as policemen, and that you knew most of the investigators, interrogators as well; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: You also said yesterday, according to the transcript and according to my memory, you repeated on two occasions during your testimony yesterday that an individual, a guard, a member of the security detail, said, told you that Mr. Kvocka was the warden. Can you tell us the name of the individual who told you that?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I should now like to address the Presiding Judge. I can give the name but in confidentiality, if confidentiality is guaranteed. But I ask for guarantees for his security.

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: Five years has passed from the war; eight years has gone by since Omarska. You can be quite certain that you have no reason not to state the name of that individual. You are testifying publicly too here today, are you not?

utterances.speaker: EDIN MRKALJ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my proposal. I am putting a concrete proposal forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Hollis, do you have any indications with respect to confidentiality, if a name is pronounced?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has expressed concerns about this person's safety who befriended him in the camp, and we would suggest that confidentiality would be appropriate in that instance, just as it is with victims and witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, do you have any objection to allow confidentiality so that the witness can give the name?

utterances.speaker: MR. K. SIMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have no objections; we agree. But I once again state that I do not consider it necessary. But we agree just to save time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are now going to go into private session to retain -- not to disclose the identity of the person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Open session].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated. We're waiting for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber has been informed by the Victims and Witnesses Unit that the witness had a slight accident yesterday. We thought it was something that happened as a consequence of these unfortunate events. We know that the witness wants to continue but it is the opinion of the Chamber that we should continue tomorrow, not today. Witness, we appreciate your willingness to continue but we feel that you are not in the best condition to testify so we're going to have a break until tomorrow, and you will continue tomorrow. In the meantime you will have a rest, the nurse or the doctor are going to treat you following the accident you had, and tomorrow we will be able to hear you. So we are going to hear you, but tomorrow. What the Chamber is going to do is to have a break in this testimony -- I'm calling it a pause respecting the will of the witness to continue -- and we will resume with the cross-examination by the Defence tomorrow at 9.30. So until tomorrow. Now, Witness, I would like you to leave before the Judges. Mr. Usher, will you escort the witness out, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the hearing is adjourned until tomorrow at 9.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: 11.28 a.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 9th day of June, 2000, at 9.30 a.m.
